title: U.S. House · Ohio's 4th District
area: North-central Ohio, including Lima and Mansfield

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 4th District R+21, a safely Republican-leaning seat.

candidates.name: Jim Jordan
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent, unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Jordan is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 4th District, first elected in 2006, and chairs the House Judiciary Committee. A former state champion and NCAA wrestling champion, he served in both chambers of the Ohio legislature before Congress, and was the first chairman of the House Freedom Caucus. He is seeking re-election.

background.text: Born in Troy, Ohio, and raised in Champaign County, Ohio; graduated from Graham High School in 1982, where, according to his congressional website, he was a four-time state wrestling champion.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin (1986), where he was a two-time NCAA wrestling champion, a master's degree from Ohio State University (1991), and a law degree from Capital University (2001).
Was an assistant wrestling coach at Ohio State University from 1987 to 1995.
Served in the Ohio House of Representatives from 1995 to 2000 and in the Ohio State Senate from 2001 to 2006.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2006 and took office in 2007, representing Ohio's 4th District.

Chaired the House Republican Study Committee in the 112th Congress and helped found the House Freedom Caucus in the 114th Congress, serving as its first chairman, according to his congressional website.
Served as ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee from 2020 to 2023 and has chaired it since January 2023; also serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
His congressional website lists recognition including Americans for Tax Reform's Friend of the Taxpayer Award and the 2012 Weyrich Award for 'National Legislator of the Year.'

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on the Judiciary and serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Kolasinski is the Democratic nominee and a business owner with an associate degree from Owens Community College and a bachelor's degree from Siena Heights University. His campaign website lists government accountability, economic opportunity for workers, and healthcare cost reform among its main policy objectives.

background.text: Earned an associate degree from Owens Community College and a bachelor's degree from Siena Heights University.
His career experience includes working as a business owner.
Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary for Ohio's 4th District; this is his first race listed on Ballotpedia.

priorities.text: Campaign website calls for government accountability and transparency, including a 'Registered Voter Lobby' and a district think tank, and says full-time work 'deserves economic stability.'
Campaign website calls for healthcare reform, including allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices and increasing price transparency.
Campaign website calls for getting 'big money out of politics,' including repealing Citizens United, banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks, and supporting term limits.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices and exploring public and private options to reduce healthcare costs.
positions.quote: Allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices. Increase price transparency so patients know costs before care.

summary.text: Tackett is the Assistant Mayor of Springfield, Ohio, where she won a seat on the City Commission in 2023, and is a development manager at Glen Helen Nature Preserve and a small-business owner. She is running as an independent, and says she is campaigning on local empowerment, fiscal responsibility and government transparency.

background.text: According to the Springfield News-Sun, grew up in Springfield, Ohio, and had volunteered in various community roles for about 20 years by 2023; she owned the downtown business Sip & Dipity for a decade and worked with Clark County Partners in Prevention.

Earned a bachelor's degree in organizational leadership and political science from Wittenberg University (2022) and a master's degree in public policy and leadership from Ohio State University's John Glenn College of Public Affairs (2024).
Ran as an independent for Clark County Commissioner in November 2022, in a race against Republican incumbent Sasha Rittenhouse and independent Dale Henry.
Won a seat on the Springfield City Commission in November 2023, defeating longtime commissioner Kevin O'Neill, 62.44% to 37.56% in unofficial results.
Serves as Assistant Mayor of Springfield; the city lists her term as ending December 31, 2027.

Describes her work as Development Manager for Glen Helen Nature Preserve as leading fundraising and community engagement for conservation and environmental education, and says she became an advocate for families navigating complex medical challenges after losing her daughter to epilepsy.

priorities.text: Says she is an independent who believes 'solving problems is more important than partisan fighting' and will work with anyone with a good idea.
priorities.quote: I'm an Independent who believes solving problems is more important than partisan fighting.

priorities.text: Says decisions should empower local governments and institutions, and pledges to 'bring resources back home, support first responders, strengthen infrastructure.'
Calls for fiscal responsibility and government transparency, and for supporting agriculture and small businesses.
